findings.detail: The new changelog entries say authenticated repeated checkpoints get the reserved SSD write share on their first local appearance. They also say short repeated prefixes below the normal solo stripe are now captured and published for reuse. T-041's detection_hint says loosening the per-donation gate (adoption bound plus 1,024-token benefit floor) widens the at-rest surface and needs review. T-041 also still says the SSD tier caches only adoptable long prefixes. If these demanded checkpoints reach SSD donation without meeting that gate, short prefixes would be written to disk and become probeable through the same-account TTFT oracle (SEC-035) for the 30-minute TTL. This is a documentation-level concern: the code is not in this batch, so I cannot confirm whether the gate applies. Fix: confirm the demanded-checkpoint path still passes the SSD adoption/benefit gate, then update T-041 and its detection_hint to record the demanded-capture path and its sign-off.
findings.title: Demanded-prefix SSD write sharing may widen T-041's per-donation gate without a sign-off
